falsifiers: n=1 mod 12 with n>10^6 not covered by residue classes
invariants: Union of residue classes mod 12 and mod 24 must cover all integers ≥3
Each residue class yields explicit (x,y,z) triple
proof_plan: Enumerate residue classes mod 12 and mod 24
For each class r, exhibit polynomial formulas for x(n),y(n),z(n)
Verify 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z symbolically for each family
Show union of classes covers all n≥3
hypotheses.rationale: Classic covering-system approach: partition integers mod 12 and 24 into residue classes, and for each class give an explicit decomposition formula. The parameters x=3,7,15,31 correspond to offsets used in the Mordell-style parametrizations for different residue classes. Most known partial results on Erdős-Straus use this strategy.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Direct encoding of the classical residue-cover approach into ESDSL1 format. The key difficulty is that residue classes mod 12 and 24 do not fully cover the hard case n≡1 mod 12.

falsifiers: Primes n≡1 mod 12 where CF convergents of 4/n do not yield valid triples
invariants: Convergent p_k/q_k of 4/n satisfies |4/n - p_k/q_k| < 1/(q_k q_{k+1})
Remainder after subtracting 1/x must itself be an Egyptian fraction of 2 terms
proof_plan: Compute continued fraction of 4/n
Extract first convergent p/q with q>n/4
Set x=q, reduce 4/n - 1/q to p'/q'
Apply greedy or divisor-pair to decompose p'/q' into 1/y+1/z
hypotheses.rationale: Use the continued fraction expansion of 4/n to find a good rational approximation 1/x, then decompose the remainder. The CF approach automatically finds denominators with small residual, potentially bypassing the hard cases of the modular sieve. Parameters encode convergent indices and trial offsets.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Synthesizes CF-based Diophantine approximation with the unit fraction decomposition problem. The approach is well-known for general Egyptian fractions but specifically tuned here for the 4/n case.

falsifiers: n prime ≡1 mod 12 where descent chain does not terminate in ≤ log(n) steps
invariants: Each descent step reduces max(x,y,z)
Descent terminates when denominator divides n exactly
Graph is acyclic for all valid n
proof_plan: Define descent operator D(n,x) = (n', x') reducing problem size
Show D preserves the Erdős-Straus equation structure
Prove termination by showing denominators decrease
Handle base cases explicitly for small n
hypotheses.rationale: Model the search for (x,y,z) as a descent on a directed graph where nodes are partial decompositions 4/n - 1/x = remainder, and edges correspond to choosing the next unit fraction. The Fibonacci-like parameters x=2,5,13,34 define preferred descent paths. Inspired by Vieta jumping and infinite descent in quadratic Diophantine equations.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Novel combination of descent methods from quadratic Diophantine theory with the linear structure of Egyptian fractions. The Fibonacci-indexed parameters aim to create descent paths with optimal convergence.

falsifiers: n where 4x-n has no divisor pair (a,b) with ab=n*x and a+b≡0 mod relevant modulus
invariants: Need divisor d of nx such that d and nx/d give valid y,z
y = nx/(4x-n) * correction terms
known_analogues: Standard divisor-pair method in Erdős-Straus literature
proof_plan: Fix x = ceil(n/4) + offset for offset in parameter set
Compute r = 4x - n
Factor nx and enumerate divisor pairs (d, nx/d)
Accept when d ≡ r mod appropriate modulus, yielding integer y,z
hypotheses.rationale: The core algebraic identity: 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z iff 4/n - 1/x = (4x-n)/(nx) = 1/y + 1/z, which requires finding divisors of nx that sum appropriately. The multi-scale moduli 12,48,144 handle different residue classes. This is the most direct algebraic approach.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Standard algebraic reformulation with extended modular sieving at three scales. The large modulus 144=12^2 attempts to resolve more subcases.

falsifiers: n where the lattice point (x,y,z) with 4yz+4xz+4xy=nxyz has no short vector
invariants: Equation 4(xy+xz+yz)=nxyz defines a lattice in (x,y,z)-space
Solutions correspond to lattice points on an algebraic surface
LLL-reduced basis should contain short solution vectors
proof_plan: Rewrite 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z as integer bilinear form
Construct lattice L_n with basis encoding the equation
Apply LLL or HKZ reduction
Extract solution from short vectors of reduced basis
hypotheses.rationale: Reinterpret the Erdős-Straus equation as finding lattice points on an algebraic surface. The equation 4(xy+xz+yz)=nxyz can be linearized by fixing x and searching for (y,z) on a hyperbola. Lattice reduction (LLL) can find short vectors corresponding to small solutions. Parameters are Sophie Germain primes chosen for their factorization difficulty.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Cross-domain transfer from computational number theory (lattice reduction) to the Egyptian fraction setting. Sophie Germain primes are chosen as they represent particularly hard cases.

falsifiers: n prime where no polynomial of degree ≤2 in n yields valid x
invariants: x(n) = (n+a)/b for class-dependent integers a,b
y and z are rational functions of n with integer values
Parametrization covers all n in given residue class
proof_plan: For each residue class mod lcm(12,60,84)=420, propose x=f(n)
Derive y(n),z(n) from the reduced equation
Verify integrality conditions
Count uncovered classes
hypotheses.rationale: Seek polynomial expressions x(n), y(n), z(n) that solve 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z for all n in a given residue class. The moduli 12,60,84 are chosen so lcm=420, giving a fine partition. Powers of 2 in x parameters encode binary search through polynomial coefficients.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Systematic polynomial ansatz with fine modular partition. The lcm=420 partition attempts to cover more cases than the classical mod 12 approach.

falsifiers: n where greedy algorithm 1/ceil(n/4) leaves remainder with no 2-term decomposition
invariants: x = ceil(n/4) + offset, offset ∈ {0,1,3,7,15}
Remainder 4/n - 1/x must be positive
Remainder denominator must factor appropriately
proof_plan: Set x = ceil(n/4) + delta for each delta in offset set
Compute remainder r/s = 4/n - 1/x in lowest terms
Check if s has divisor d with d ≡ -s/r mod (s/r)
If yes, extract y,z; if no, try next delta
hypotheses.rationale: The greedy algorithm for Egyptian fractions chooses x=ceil(n/4), which works for many n. When it fails, small offsets can rescue the decomposition. The offsets 0,1,3,7,15 (Mersenne-like) are chosen to maximize the chance that the remainder has a convenient factorization. This is the computational baseline with systematic offset exploration.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Elaboration of the known greedy baseline with Mersenne-indexed offsets. Simple but effective for covering most cases.

falsifiers: n≡1 mod 24 where sieve leaves no admissible (x,y,z)
invariants: For each prime p in sieve, n mod p determines feasibility
Intersection of feasible classes must be non-empty
Sieve density remains positive as moduli grow
proof_plan: For each modulus m, classify residues of n into easy/hard
Apply inclusion-exclusion to bound density of hard cases
Show hard case density → 0 as sieve depth increases
Explicitly handle any surviving hard residue classes
hypotheses.rationale: Apply sieve methods from analytic number theory to the Erdős-Straus problem. For each prime modulus p, determine which residue classes of n allow easy decompositions. The sieve parameters are primes chosen for their coverage efficiency. The key question is whether the sieve density of hard cases can be driven to zero.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Transfers sieve methodology from prime counting to Egyptian fraction feasibility. The choice of prime moduli 5,17,41,97 aims for near-independent coverage.

falsifiers: n≡1 mod 840 not covered by any residue class in the system
invariants: Covering system uses moduli dividing lcm(12,60,168)=840
Each residue class mod 840 maps to an explicit triple
x values follow the pattern 4(2^k-1) for parametric flexibility
proof_plan: Enumerate all 840 residue classes
For each class, try x = n*f(r)/g(r) for class-specific rational functions
Verify integrality and positivity
Catalog uncovered classes and attempt secondary covers
hypotheses.rationale: Extend the classical covering system approach to modulus 840 = 2^3 * 3 * 5 * 7, which is much larger than the usual 12 or 24. The x-values 4,12,28,60,124 follow 4(2^k-1) and provide geometrically spaced trial denominators. With 840 classes, far more cases can be resolved by direct polynomial parametrization.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Aggressive scaling of the covering system approach. Whether mod 840 suffices to cover all cases is unknown, but it dramatically reduces the number of hard cases.

falsifiers: Mersenne prime n where hyperbola has no integer point in the lattice
invariants: For fixed x, equation becomes (4x-n)yz = nx(y+z)
This defines a hyperbola in (y,z)-plane
Integer points on hyperbola ↔ divisors of nx^2/(4x-n)^2
known_analogues: Pell equation solution via lattice methods
proof_plan: Fix x from parameter set (values are 2(2^k-1))
Transform to hyperbola (4x-n)(y-A)(z-A)=A^2*nx for appropriate A
Search for lattice points using Cornacchia-like algorithm
Combine solutions across different x values
hypotheses.rationale: After fixing x, the remaining equation in y,z defines a hyperbola. Finding integer points on this hyperbola is equivalent to factoring a specific integer. The lattice transform approach uses the geometry of the hyperbola to systematically enumerate solutions. Mersenne-like x values 6,14,30,62 create hyperbolas with special arithmetic properties.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Combines the algebraic structure of the reduced 2-variable problem with lattice point enumeration on conics. The specific x-values create hyperbolas whose discriminants have controlled factorization.

falsifiers: n for which the generating function coefficient extraction yields no valid triple
invariants: G(q) = sum_{n>=3} f(n) q^n where f(n) counts decompositions
Fibonacci-indexed coefficients have special modularity
Non-vanishing of f(n) equivalent to Erdős-Straus for n
known_analogues: Generating function approach to partition problems
proof_plan: Define G(q) = sum over valid triples of q^n weight
Factor G using modular forms / theta function identities
Show G has no zero coefficients for n≥3
Extract constructive decomposition from dominant term

The Fibonacci parameters 2,3,5,8,13 index special evaluation points where the generating function has analytic structure amenable to the circle method. Modulus 144=12^2 provides a fine-grained modular decomposition of the generating function.
hypotheses.synthesis_note: Highly speculative transfer of circle method ideas to the Egyptian fraction counting problem. The Fibonacci indexing is motivated by golden-ratio-related convergence properties.

falsifiers: n≡1 mod 9 where ternary expansion yields no valid parametrization
invariants: x values are powers of 3: 3^1,...,3^5
For n≡0 mod 3, trivial: 4/n = 1/(n/3) + 1/(n/3) + 1/(2n/3) type
Ternary structure exploits 3-adic valuation of n

For each valuation, choose x = 3^k with k = v_3(n)+1
Reduce to equation over integers coprime to 3
Apply Hensel-like lifting to construct y,z from mod-9 solutions

hard_1_mod_12.search_rule: x ascending from n//4 + 1 with a small-divisor y window per x (64 x-rounds, 32 y-offsets, exact int64), then a complete per-x divisor search of b^2 on the CPU; x_offset is schedule-relative

results.witness_storage: full witness tables (~n_max rows) are deliberately not stored: counts per class, deterministic strided samples, and schedule-relative extremal minimal-x witnesses only; every stored witness is exactly verified and every hard-class witness was exactly verified during the run

finite_sweep.scope: Generalized exponent-Diophantine sweep of one declared finite box for one queue v3 target; this module is the diophantine_family sweeper whose absence discovery receipts record as the typed blocker missing_sweeper:diophantine_family. The fp64 log-space layer (GPU or numpy) is a screen only, admitted after an a-priori resolution proof that guarantees every true solution is flagged; every near-hit is settled with exact Python big-integer arithmetic and the receipt records the near-hit -> exact funnel. Beal solutions carry exact gcds: a coprime confirmation is a COUNTEREXAMPLE_CANDIDATE with mandatory independent re-verification, while known gcd > 1 families are the rediscovery control. Fermat-Catalan confirmations are matched by power values against the builtin ten-solution table; unmatched confirmations claim no novelty. Erdos-Straus witnesses come from symbolically verified parametric identities on four residue classes plus an exact GPU-assisted search on n = 1 (mod 12), stored as counts, deterministic samples, and schedule-relative extremal witnesses, never full tables. A finite box proves nothing outside itself; every mode's box sits below its documented literature landscape, so these are mechanism receipts and the claims blocks say so.
